market_view: South African shares slipped 0.3% as Woolworths' stalled food sales outweighed Vodacom's strong interim results, and the rand fell to a seven-month low near R17/$ ahead of October CPI on 18 Nov and the MPC on 19 Nov, where a hike from 7.25% is being debated. In New York the S&P 500 still gained 2.5% for its best week since August, but the 10-year Treasury yield jumped about 30bp to 5.15% as hot October CPI and PPI data and Fed talk of a 50bp move left a December hike fully priced, while Friday's chip sell-off after Nvidia's CEO change showed how fragile tech leadership has become. Gold fell 4.6% to about $3,886 and Brent 2.5% to $96 while iron ore held near $91, so investors should prepare for higher-for-longer rates to keep pressure on the rand, bonds and precious-metal miners, favouring companies with pricing power and dollar earnings.
